name: Decoding brain signals and neural activity
gist: Translating brain scans, EEG, and neural recordings into readable signals—what someone is thinking, intending, or perceiving—opening new ways to understand and help the brain.
explain: When you think, your brain's neurons fire in patterns. When you move your hand, specific motor neurons activate. Researchers can record these electrical signals using electrodes (EEG, implanted sensors) or infer them from imaging (fMRI, PET). But the signals are noisy, and the brain is so complicated that no one has figured out a simple rule that translates the neural firing pattern into what you are thinking or wanting to do.

The challenge is that each person's brain is wired differently, the recording setup changes between sessions, and the same thought might activate different neurons at different times. A model that works for one person might completely fail for another. Yet the payoff is huge: if we can decode intention from brain signals, paralyzed people could control prosthetics with their thoughts, locked-in patients could communicate, and neuroscientists could understand how the brain encodes information.

This cluster trains neural networks to map from brain signals to behavior or intention. Some decode motor cortex recordings to predict which direction a person is planning to move, so a prosthetic arm can move before the person finishes the thought. Others decode visual cortex to reconstruct what someone is looking at or imagining. Still others use the signals to classify what a person is thinking about or predict their next decision. The technical challenge is working with small datasets (brain experiments are expensive and time-consuming), handling the unique wiring of each subject, and building models that can adapt to new people quickly. Papers here use transfer learning, personalization techniques, and carefully chosen network architectures that respect the structure of the brain.

papers.title: Beyond Grid-Locked Voxels: Neural Response Functions for Continuous Brain Encoding
papers.contribution: Outperforms baseline models in intrasubject encoding and cross-subject adaptation while reducing required data by orders of magnitude.

papers.title: ECHO: Toward Contextual Seq2Seq Paradigms in Large EEG Models
papers.contribution: ECHO outperforms state-of-the-art single-task LEMs in multi-task settings, showing superior generalization and adaptability across multiple datasets.

papers.title: Model-Guided Microstimulation Steers Primate Visual Behavior
papers.contribution: Model-guided stimulation successfully steers complex visual behavior in macaques, establishing a foundation for next-generation prosthetics targeting higher-level visual cortex.

papers.title: Training Deep Normalization-Free Spiking Neural Networks with Lateral Inhibition
papers.contribution: Enables stable training of deep normalization-free SNNs with biological realism while achieving competitive performance without explicit normalization.

papers.title: Biologically Plausible Learning via Bidirectional Spike-Based Distillation
papers.contribution: BSD achieves performance comparable to error backpropagation across image recognition, generation, and sequential regression on diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: Continuous multinomial logistic regression for neural decoding
papers.contribution: CMLR consistently outperforms DNNs, XGBoost, and FlexCode on large-scale neural datasets from mouse/monkey visual and motor cortex, capturing multimodal and asymmetric distributions.

papers.title: Emergence of Spatial Representation in an Actor-Critic Agent with Hippocampus-Inspired Sequence Generator
papers.contribution: Shows that sparse input synergizes with sequence-generating dynamics to enable maze navigation, with emergent spatial phenomena aligning with neurobiological data.

papers.title: HEEGNet: Hyperbolic Embeddings for EEG
papers.contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate HEEGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple EEG datasets covering visual evoked potentials, emotion recognition, and intracranial EEG.

papers.title: Hyperbolic neural population geometry benefits computation
papers.contribution: The hyperbolic memory model yields significantly larger capacity than leading models while improving both memory capacity and decoding accuracy.

papers.title: Mind the State: Towards Unified, Context-Aware EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
papers.contribution: Reliably reconstructs temporally-resolved whole-brain fMRI from EEG with potential for zero-shot generalization to task-based fMRI and clinical populations.

papers.title: MnemoDyn: Learning Resting State Dynamics from $40$K FMRI sequences
papers.contribution: MnemoDyn delivers superior reconstruction quality compared to state-of-the-art transformer-based approaches and generalizes well across populations and protocols while being compute efficient.
